races.title: State House, District 105
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Tricia Ann Cotham
cands.bio: Republican state representative for North Carolina House District 105. Former Charlotte-Mecklenburg Schools teacher, assistant principal and athletic coach, and a business owner. Served in the NC House from 2007 to 2016 (District 100) and again from 2023 (Districts 112, then 105). Switched from Democrat to Republican in April 2023.
cands.gaps: We could not find her birthplace, where she grew up, or when she came to North Carolina. We found no documented actions or stated positions of hers on data centers, homestead property taxes, land ownership, growth and land protection, immigration and H-1B, campaign donor pledges, policing, gun policy, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. Ballotpedia lists no sponsored bills in the text we could read, and she did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys in 2022, 2024 or 2026. Ballotpedia identified no endorsements for her in 2024 or 2026, and her campaign site's endorsements section had no content. We found no land-use positions or news controversies beyond her April 2023 party switch.

cands.name: Ken McCool
cands.bio: Ken McCool, 28, is a Matthews, N.C. small-business owner who runs a sports cards and collectibles store. He served on the Matthews Board of Commissioners for three terms, including as mayor pro tem. He is a Democrat who defeated incumbent Tricia Cotham in the 2026 race for N.C. House District 105.

endorsements.text: Charlotte-area Fraternal Order of Police lodge (per his campaign site and Wikipedia).

Candidate-reported endorsements include NCAE, Carolina Forward, Now or Never NC, Work for Democracy NC, State Sen. Woodson Bradley, several Democratic state House members, former Rep. Wiley Nickel and Matthews Mayor John Higdon. This list comes from his own survey answers.

cands.gaps: We could not find his birthplace or any record of when, or whether, he lived outside North Carolina. We found no independent record of his Matthews town board votes, so his claims about affordable housing, parks, public safety and the Hendrick Advanced Manufacturing Campus rest on his own statements. We found no stated positions from him on data centers, growth and land limits, homestead property tax elimination, foreign or institutional land buying, immigration or H-1B, guns, or abortion. We found no controversies, no documented foreign ties and no official records of his time in office.

local.label: Roots 90: He describes himself as a lifelong Matthews resident and a Providence High School graduate, so he was raised in North Carolina, but his birthplace is not stated in the sources.

qual.background: He served three terms on the Matthews town board (including as mayor pro tem) and owns a sports cards and collectibles store. He studied journalism. He has no prior state legislative service.
qual.why: Local elected office plus small-business ownership fits the middle band. He has no state legislative or budget-career experience, and his town-board work is mostly self-reported.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Says legislators have promoted "unregulated private school vouchers" that leave public schools behind, and says he will fight to fully fund public schools. He also says teachers are underpaid, but he gives no specific raise figure.

back-police-order.evidence: Says he strongly supported a first responder training facility at CPCC's Levine Campus and the construction of Matthews Fire Station 3 while on the town council. He lists public safety as a priority and cites the Fraternal Order of Police endorsement. These are his own claims, not independently checked.
